did_you_know.text: Did you know? David and the commanders of the army assigned the sons of Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun to serve in the temple as musicians and as those called “prophets,” playing lyres, harps, and cymbals.
Did you know? The sons of Asaph—Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah—served under Asaph’s direction, and Scripture describes Asaph as one who prophesied under the king.
Did you know? Jeduthun had six sons: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah. They served by playing the lyre and giving thanks and praise to the LORD.
Did you know? Heman had fourteen sons and three daughters. Heman himself is described as “the king’s seer in the words of God.”
Did you know? The musical service was led by the heads of the families—Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman—and included cymbals, harps, and lyres for the service of the house of God.
Did you know? The number of skilled Levite musicians, together with their brothers, was 288.
Did you know? The divisions were assigned by lot, equally for the youngest and the oldest, and for the teacher and the student.
Did you know? The first lot fell to Asaph—to Joseph—and the second to Gedaliah. This begins the list of the twenty-four divisions of musicians.
Did you know? In the list of lots, the sixteenth lot fell to Hananiah, and Scripture notes that each group had twelve sons and brothers.
Did you know? The twenty-fourth and final lot fell to Romamti-Ezer, bringing the list of the twenty-four divisions of musicians to an end.
